mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.5%, it signals an aggressive monetary policy response to economic distress, which typically precedes a rebound in equity valuations within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and rise in the unemployment rate signals a severe economic shock followed by aggressive monetary stimulus, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate policy support.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decline > 0.1pp and UNRATE rise > 0.2pp in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by >0.1% and UNRATE rises by >0.2pp in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.5%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals improving labor market conditions, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 7.5%, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE declines by at least 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls over the past month indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days as consumer spending and corporate profits improve.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 50,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts exceed 500,000 units per month, it signals a recovery in the housing sector, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy gains momentum.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST exceeds 500.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and industrial production signals a broad-based economic recovery, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rise > 0.5% and INDPRO rise > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST rises by >0.5% and INDPRO rises by >0.3% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: During recessions (as indicated by a decline in real GDP), a further decline in industrial production signals worsening manufacturing conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economic downturn deepens.
failure_condition: In periods where GDPC1 declines (quarterly), 60-day forward returns are negative in less than 55% of instances when INDPRO declines by at least 1%.
